## Introduction

This example won **The Best Pharma Table** category of the
[2025 Posit Table Contest](https://posit.co/blog/2025-table-contest-winners/).

- Contest submission:
  [Submission-Ready and Elegant Clinical Tables: Combining {gt} Styling with {gridify} Layout Control](https://github.com/rich-iannone/table-contest/discussions/18)
- Original code: [Polkas/tgcontest2025](https://github.com/Polkas/tgcontest2025)

Clinical reporting requires tables that meet both statistical rigour and
regulatory standards. While pharmaverse packages handle the analysis well,
a gap remains in the consistent and reproducible framing of Tables, Listings,
and Graphs (TLGs) with the headers, footers, compliance notices, and metadata
required for submissions.

This example combines `gt` for table styling with `gridify` for
regulatory-compliant framing. The table shows a CDISC ADSL baseline
characteristic, Biomarker 1 (`BMRKR1`), by treatment arm and geographic
region with:

- summary statistics: n and Mean (SD), with gradient colour encoding,
- complete regulatory framing: protocol information, data cut-off,
  confidentiality notice, and traceability.

All data are synthetic, generated by the `random.cdisc.data` package.
No real patient data are used, and the company, study, and drug
information are fictional.

## Setup

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(gridify)
library(gt)
library(dplyr)

primary_color <- "#08306b"
secondary_color <- "#6baed6"
```

## Data Preparation

The ADSL dataset is summarised by treatment arm and region.
The `BMRKR1` column is stored as a factor ordered by the mean value,
so that the colour gradient applied later follows the mean.

```{r data}
adsl <- random.cdisc.data::cadsl |>
  mutate(
    ARM = factor(ARM),
    REGION1 = factor(REGION1)
  )

summary_tbl <- adsl |>
  group_by(ARM, REGION1) |>
  summarise(
    N = n(),
    MEAN_BMRKR1 = round(mean(BMRKR1, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    SD_BMRKR1 = round(sd(BMRKR1, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    BMRKR1 = sprintf("%0.2f (%0.2f)", MEAN_BMRKR1, SD_BMRKR1),
    BMRKR1 = factor(BMRKR1, levels = unique(BMRKR1[order(MEAN_BMRKR1)]))
  ) |>
  select(ARM, REGION1, N, BMRKR1)

summary_tbl
```

## The gt Table

```{r gt_table}
color_palette <- scales::col_factor(
  palette = c("white", secondary_color, primary_color),
  domain = NULL
)

gt_tbl <- summary_tbl |>
  gt(rowname_col = NULL, groupname_col = "ARM") |>
  cols_label(
    REGION1 = "Region",
    N = "n",
    BMRKR1 = "BMRKR1"
  ) |>
  cols_width(
    ARM ~ pct(30),
    REGION1 ~ pct(30),
    N ~ pct(10),
    BMRKR1 ~ pct(30)
  ) |>
  cols_align(
    align = "center",
    columns = N
  ) |>
  tab_options(
    table.width = pct(70),
    table.font.size = 16,
    data_row.padding = px(6),
    table.font.color = "black",
    table.font.weight = "400",
    heading.align = "left",
    table.background.color = "gray98",
    heading.background.color = "gray98",
    column_labels.background.color = "gray95",
    row_group.font.weight = "bold",
    row_group.as_column = TRUE
  ) |>
  opt_row_striping() |>
  data_color(columns = BMRKR1, fn = color_palette) |>
  data_color(columns = N, fn = color_palette) |>
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(weight = "bold", color = primary_color),
    locations = cells_column_labels()
  )
```

## Framing with gridify

The `gt` table is passed to `gridify()` with the predefined
`pharma_layout_base()` layout. Custom margins and a monospaced font are
used, and the cells are filled with `set_cell()`.

```{r gridify}
pharma_gt <- gridify(
  gt_tbl,
  layout = pharma_layout_base(
    margin = grid::unit(c(t = 0.5, r = 0.5, b = 0.5, l = 0.5), "inch"),
    global_gpar = list(
      fontfamily = "mono",
      fontsize = 14,
      col = "black"
    )
  )
) |>
  set_cell("header_left_1", "PharmaCorp International") |>
  set_cell("header_left_2", "ONCOLOGY / Advanced NSCLC") |>
  set_cell("header_left_3", "Study PC-2025-001") |>
  set_cell("header_right_1", "CONFIDENTIAL") |>
  set_cell("header_right_2", "Final") |>
  set_cell("header_right_3", "Data Cut-off: 2025-09-30") |>
  set_cell("output_num", "Table 14.1.1") |>
  set_cell("title_1", "Summary of Demographics and Baseline Characteristics") |>
  set_cell("title_2", "Baseline Biomarker 1 (BMRKR1) by Geographic Region") |>
  set_cell("title_3", "Safety Analysis Set") |>
  set_cell("note", "Note: BMRKR1 values shown as Mean (SD).") |>
  set_cell("references", "Source: ADSL dataset random.cdisc.data") |>
  set_cell("footer_left", "Program: table_posit.R, 2025-10-01 12:00 UTC") |>
  set_cell("footer_right", "Page 1 of 1")

pharma_gt
```

In a production program, the `footer_left` cell would typically contain
the run time, e.g.
`sprintf("Program: table_posit.R, %s", format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M %Z"))`.

## Export

The final output can be exported to PNG or PDF with `export_to()`.

```{r export, eval = FALSE}
pharma_gt |>
  export_to("polkas_table_contest_2025.png", width = 3000, height = 2600, res = 300)

pharma_gt |>
  export_to("polkas_table_contest_2025.pdf")
```

To retrieve the raw `grid` code behind the output, see
`vignette("transparency", package = "gridify")`.
